math_review.uv_gradient: For det=duA*dvB-duB*dvA, dP/dU=(edgeA*dvB-edgeB*dvA)/det and dP/dV=(edgeB*duA-edgeA*duB)/det are the correct inverse UV-gradient solution. Both triangle edges are reconstructed by those derivatives when det is nondegenerate.
math_review.frame: Each authored normal is normalized locally for the calculation; tangent is Gram–Schmidt projected dP/dU onto its perpendicular plane, then normalized. The original normal stream is not rewritten. W=-1 when dot(cross(N,T),dP/dV)<0, otherwise+1, consistently selecting UV bitangent orientation for nondegenerate gradients.
math_review.fallback: Collapsed/near-zero UV determinant leaves zero gradients. A tiny projected tangent selects projected UP for abs(normal.y)<0.9, otherwise RIGHT. For current finite unit nonzero authored normals these axes cannot be parallel; projected lengths are bounded away from zero before normalization. Degenerate UVs have no unique UV handedness, so fallback W=+1 is a stable frame, not equivalence to an authored UV derivative.
